profiles.summary: The stakely.io rotation is now counted: of 500 three-call batches in two samples, 286 came from 7680d6d (celo/reth-v1.0.0 or v1.0.1), 173 from 74cc8bb (v1.0.9 or v1.0.10) and 41 from 06140ff (v1.0.6 to v1.0.8); 3cbf835 (v1.0.3) answered none of those but 307 of the eth_call batches of the pinned run, and every batch was answered whole by one backend. Celo builds have no keccak cache in front of KECCAK256, and the engine precompile cache leaves the transfer precompile out.

deltas.delta: stakely.io answers most requests from the oldest public celo-reth build: 286 of 500 batches from reth/v2.2.0-7680d6d, 173 from 74cc8bb, 41 from 06140ff and none from 3cbf835, in runs of 11 to 66 consecutive batches, while 3cbf835 answered 307 eth_call batches of the pinned vector run; celo.api.onfinality.io/public answered 7680d6d to 4 of 4 calls. forno answered 253 of 300 batches from reth 74cc8bb and 47 from the op-geth build c7ed55b8.
deltas.source: https://celo-json-rpc.stakely.io (500 JSON-RPC batches of three web3_clientVersion calls in two samples, 2026-11-27, out/rotation-stakely.json and out/rotation-stakely-2.json)

deltas.delta: The celo-reth v1.0.10 lock has no fixed-cache crate, so alloy-primitives 1.6.0 is built without the keccak-cache features and KECCAK256 is computed on every call. The build uses keccak-asm 0.1.6 with sha3-asm 0.1.6, and the Celo Dockerfile sets no target-cpu, so the plain x86_64 CRYPTOGAMS keccak is assembled.

The engine precompile cache of celo-reth 74cc8bb (moka cache per address keyed by input bytes and spec, gas checked against the cached gas used) wraps only precompiles whose supports_caching is true; alloy-celo-evm builds the transfer precompile at 0xfd with .stateful(), so it always executes.

The 06140ff build was pinned for the four vector sets on stakely.io: returned the specified word on 20400 of 215637 vectors pinned before the run was stopped (34 of 360 batches, 0 mismatches; while it ran, the eth_call batches were answered 2654 times by 74cc8bb, 1830 by 7680d6d, 307 by 3cbf835 and 34 by 06140ff).
deltas.source: https://celo-json-rpc.stakely.io (eth_call with code override between two web3_clientVersion calls, 2026-11-27, out/celo-06140ff-stakely-all.json)

profiles.summary: Nothing new on transaction boundaries. Celo reth returns the revert data of a failed simulated call in returnData rather than in error.data, which only changes how eth_simulateV1 results are read.

deltas.delta: eth_simulateV1 on reth 74cc8bb puts revert data of failed calls in returnData with error code 3 and no error.data; the cycle 29 comparison script reads error.data and saw four false differences in scenario E1 that disappear when returnData is read.

profiles.summary: Nothing new. The Celo network notices still list only the op-geth end of support and the CL sync deprecation, and no Karst notice or date exists.

Nothing new on predeploys: 0x4200..0029 to 0x4200..002D hold the 2,059 byte proxy with implementation slot zero and balance zero at block 83,848,106. The two copies of the transfer precompile (handler path in celo-revm and DynPrecompile path in alloy-celo-evm) apply the same checks in the same order.

X Layer computes KECCAK256 through a process-wide cache: xlayer-reth takes the okx/reth bin crate with default features, which include keccak-cache-global, so alloy-primitives 1.6.0 serves every hash of 1 to 87 bytes from a 131,072-entry fixed-cache 0.1.10 table shared by RPC and block execution. The cache compares the full input under a per-bucket lock, and 13,488 cache-shaped vectors returned the specified hash.

deltas.delta: The xlayer-reth workspace pins reth = okx/reth f60420a without default-features = false; okx/reth bin/reth defaults include keccak-cache-global and asm-keccak, which turn on alloy-primitives/keccak-cache-global. The lock carries fixed-cache 0.1.10 as an alloy-primitives dependency, which the Celo lock does not.

alloy-primitives 1.6.0 keccak256() sends inputs of 1 to 87 bytes (MAX_INPUT_LEN = 128 - 32 - 1 - 8) to a static one-way set associative cache of 2^17 buckets keyed by rapidhash; revm-interpreter 37.0.3 KECCAK256 calls primitives::keccak256 (instructions/system.rs:36), so every mapping slot, transient delta slot and position key of the PoolManager goes through it.

sha3-asm 0.1.8 picks the CRYPTOGAMS keccak at build time: keccak1600-avx512vl when the target has avx512vl, plain keccak1600-x86_64 otherwise or on a Zen 5 target. The project justfile recipes build-maxperf and install-maxperf set RUSTFLAGS=-C target-cpu=native, while DockerfileOp passes empty RUSTFLAGS by default, so an operator who installs with the justfile on an AVX-512 machine runs a different keccak routine from the public endpoint.

profiles.summary: Nothing new on transaction boundaries. eth_simulateV1 is refused on rpc.xlayer.tech, xlayerrpc.okx.com and 196.rpc.thirdweb.com and served by xlayer.drpc.org, which reports its gateway string and cannot be tied to a build.
Nothing new. No X Layer hard fork is listed after the 10 November 2026 mainnet hard fork, and Lagoon lists only OP Mainnet, Unichain, Ink and Soneium.

The engine precompile cache of okx/reth f60420a was read: it wraps the stock OP Stack precompiles, keys entries by input bytes and spec, checks the caller gas against the cached gas used, and stores only successful results.

deltas.delta: okx/reth f60420a wraps cacheable precompiles in both the prewarm path and the main block validation path (payload_validator.rs:1072-1084); alloy-evm marks every precompile cacheable except identity and those built stateful.

findings.title: Celo public endpoints answer most reads from superseded celo-reth releases, one of them older than a consensus fix
findings.difference: On Celo the stakely.io endpoint answers from four reth builds and onfinality from one, and the most frequent of them is the oldest public release. In 500 batches stakely.io answered 286 from 7680d6d (celo/reth-v1.0.0 or v1.0.1), 173 from 74cc8bb (v1.0.9 or v1.0.10) and 41 from 06140ff (v1.0.6 to v1.0.8). 3cbf835 (v1.0.3) answered none of the version-only batches but 307 of the eth_call batches of the pinned vector run, so it is still in the rotation. 7680d6d predates the v1.0.4 change that makes a zero-address feeCurrency an unregistered currency and adds the CIP-64 rule balanceOf(caller) >= gasLimit * maxFeePerGas.
findings.mechanism: A wallet, router or quoter that reads the PoolManager through these endpoints gets an eth_call answer from whichever build serves the batch. Each batch is served whole by one backend (0 mixed batches of 500), and the backend changes in runs of 11 to 66 batches. All four builds lock revm-interpreter 35.0.1 and ruint 1.18.0 or 1.20.0. Pinned this way every build returned the specified word on every vector it was pinned to: 7680d6d on 214,437 of 215,637 vectors in cycle 28, 3cbf835 on 4,200 in cycle 28, 74cc8bb on all sets, and 06140ff this cycle, which returned the specified word on 20400 of 215637 vectors pinned before the run was stopped (34 of 360 batches, 0 mismatches; while it ran, the eth_call batches were answered 2654 times by 74cc8bb, 1830 by 7680d6d, 307 by 3cbf835 and 34 by 06140ff). The three getFeeGrowthInside borrow scripts (src/libraries/Pool.sol:498-509) gave the reference record on 7680d6d and 74cc8bb, and the 23 multi-transaction scenarios gave the reference outputs on 7680d6d (22 of 23 scenarios identical (90608 bytes compared), not identical: E1; E1 differs only in where revert data is reported) and on 74cc8bb. The builds differ in CIP-64 admission and pricing of simulated fees, which no PoolManager line reads. Blocks come from the Celo sequencer. 7680d6d and 3cbf835 are the looser builds: they accept every transaction the v1.0.4 rule accepts, and more, so a follower on one of them never rejects a block from a sequencer on v1.0.4 or later. A split needs a sequencer on an old build that includes a transaction the v1.0.4 rule rejects; the newer followers would then reject that block, as op-geth did at block 75,046,581.
findings.impact: No PoolManager funds move and no withdrawal is blocked. A user relying on 7680d6d may see a CIP-64 simulation priced differently from the chain, or a zero-address feeCurrency transaction accepted by that node and then rejected.
findings.preconditions: The user reads or simulates through stakely.io or onfinality. A divergent block needs a sequencer that runs one of the old builds.
findings.mitigations: Integrators should check web3_clientVersion and read the PoolManager through an endpoint that reports reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb or later; Celo can ask providers to retire builds older than v1.0.4.

On both builds E1 differs only at transactions 3 to 6, the four reverts that carry data, because Celo reth returns revert data in returnData and the comparison reads error.data; with returnData read all ten outputs equal the reference (out/e1-celo-publicnode.json, out/e1-celo-stakely.json). X Layer through drpc: 23 of 23 scenarios identical (90608 bytes compared). The Geth c7ed55b8 backend has no public endpoint that serves eth_simulateV1, so the scenarios did not run on it.

cleared.check: Whether the global keccak cache in front of KECCAK256 on X Layer (alloy-primitives 1.6.0 keccak_cache.rs with fixed-cache 0.1.10) can return a hash for an input other than the one asked, which would change every pool, tick, position and delta slot the PoolManager computes (src/types/PoolId.sol:14 is 160 bytes and bypasses it; src/libraries/Position.sol:60 at 58 bytes, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:14 at 64 bytes and every compiler-generated mapping slot at 64 bytes go through it).
cleared.result: No. The key stores the length and the bytes, and equality compares the full slice (keccak_cache.rs lines 80-113). get_or_insert_with_ref locks the bucket only when its tag word equals the computed tag, compares the stored key with the input under that lock, and otherwise computes keccak256 of the input itself and inserts it (fixed-cache lib.rs get_inner, insert_inner and try_lock_ret, Acquire on lock and Release on unlock). An empty bucket has key length zero and the empty input never reaches the cache. A hash collision or a racing writer can only cause a miss. Any account can evict entries through eth_call or transactions, which changes speed only. 13,488 KECCAK256 vectors (every length 1 to 96 at eight offsets, inputs that share a prefix and differ only in length, all-zero and one-bit inputs, 64 byte mapping and 58 byte position shapes, each set sent twice so the second round hits a warm cache) returned the specified hash on f60420a, and 6,744 of them on Celo reth 74cc8bb, which has no cache: 0 and 0 mismatches.

cleared.check: The engine precompile cache (crates/engine/tree/src/tree/precompile_cache.rs) of okx/reth f60420a and celo-org/reth 74cc8bb, listed in OPCODES.md as unread: whether a cached result can be returned for a call the precompile would answer differently, or whether a stateful precompile is cached.
cleared.result: Entries are kept per precompile address, keyed by the full input bytes and filtered by spec; a hit also needs the caller gas to be at least the cached gas used, and only successful outputs that did not touch the reservoir or state gas are stored. The two files differ only in an initial_capacity line. map_cacheable_precompiles in alloy-evm 0.34.0 skips identity and any precompile marked stateful, and alloy-celo-evm marks the Celo transfer precompile with .stateful(), so a CELO token transfer always moves balances. The PoolManager reads no precompile result in its own math; a pool whose currency is the CELO token reaches the transfer precompile only through the token contract.

cleared.check: The two copies of the Celo transfer precompile: celo-revm precompiles/transfer.rs (handler path) and alloy-celo-evm lib.rs transfer_precompile (DynPrecompile path used by reth execution and eth_call), whose comment says they must be kept in sync.
cleared.result: Both halt in a static context, halt with out of gas below 9,000, require the caller to be the chain's CELO token, require exactly 96 bytes, read from, to and value from the same offsets, restore the cold status of from and to before Jovian, move value with the journal transfer and halt on a transfer or database error. No difference in order or bounds was found.

cleared.check: The keccak assembly behind KECCAK256: sha3-asm 0.1.6 (Celo) against 0.1.8 (X Layer), and which CRYPTOGAMS routine each released build assembles.
cleared.result: Both choose the routine at build time from target features. With the default x86_64 target, as in the Celo Dockerfile (RUSTFLAGS only adds frame pointers and line tables) and the X Layer DockerfileOp (empty RUSTFLAGS), both assemble keccak1600-x86_64. 0.1.8 changes symbol renaming for the _neon and _kimd suffixes, fixes patch matching by exact stem and puts Zen 5 on the plain routine; none of it changes the plain x86_64 routine. The battery KECCAK256 vectors and the 13,488 cache vectors exercise the endpoint build. The avx512vl routine a target-cpu=native build would choose was not executed; see the lead.

cleared.check: Upcoming forks within six months, assumed to ship: anything scheduled for Celo or X Layer, and Lagoon.
cleared.result: Celo network notices list no hardfork (only the op-geth end of support and the CL sync deprecation), and celo-kona has no tag after celo/reth-v1.0.10. X Layer lists no upgrade after the 10 November 2026 mainnet hard fork, and xlayer-reth has no tag after v0.0.7.3-rc.1. Lagoon lists OP Mainnet, Unichain, Ink and Soneium for 11 January 2027 and neither of these chains. With nothing scheduled, the PoolManager and its funds see no change from a fork in this window; Karst on Celo stays the open item (L-980).

leads.why: F-160 rests on followers; a divergence from the v1.0.4 rule needs the sequencer to include a transaction the old builds accept.

leadResults.answer: Borrow scripts: Geth c7ed55b8 3 of 3 equal, reth 74cc8bb 3 of 3 equal, reth 7680d6d 3 of 3 equal, X Layer f60420a 3 of 3 equal, each call pinned by clientVersion brackets. scen28: eth_simulateV1 is refused on forno and rpc.xlayer.tech, so Celo ran on publicnode 74cc8bb (22 of 23 scenarios identical (90608 bytes compared), not identical: E1; E1 differs only in where revert data is reported), stakely 7680d6d (22 of 23 scenarios identical (90608 bytes compared), not identical: E1) and X Layer through drpc (23 of 23 scenarios identical (90608 bytes compared), build not tied). The 15,510 large-index vectors were already pinned to Geth c7ed55b8, reth 74cc8bb and f60420a in cycle 28 (L-1156). The Geth backend has no simulateV1 endpoint.

In 500 three-element batches to stakely.io on 2026-11-27, in two samples: 7680d6d answered 286, 74cc8bb 173, 06140ff 41 and 3cbf835 0; no batch mixed builds. During the pinned vector run 3cbf835 answered 307 eth_call batches, so all four builds of cycle 28 are still served. 06140ff answered runs of 12, 13 and 16 consecutive batches, and runs of all builds were 11 to 66 batches long; pinned to it: returned the specified word on 20400 of 215637 vectors pinned before the run was stopped (34 of 360 batches, 0 mismatches; while it ran, the eth_call batches were answered 2654 times by 74cc8bb, 1830 by 7680d6d, 307 by 3cbf835 and 34 by 06140ff). The verifier's two-build sample was a short window of the same rotation, whose runs last 11 to 66 batches.

Not searched again this cycle, which went to the interpreter and the caches in front of it. The F-144 shape concerns the CIP-64 refund and touches no PoolManager line; cycle 28 found no mined candidate in 20,000 blocks.

No celo-reth tag carries revm 42 yet; the newest tag is still celo/reth-v1.0.10 (revm 38.0.0, revm-interpreter 35.0.1 from celo-org/revm bd28f942). onfinality still answers reth/v2.2.0-7680d6d, which is celo/reth-v1.0.0 or v1.0.1, and stakely.io answered 286 of 500 batches from it.

Karst still has no Celo notice or date and no tag after celo/reth-v1.0.10 exists. At block 83,848,106 the predeploys 0x4200..0029 to 0x4200..002D hold the 2,059 byte proxy with EIP-1967 implementation slot zero and balance zero (out/celo-predeploys.json). The post-activation sweep stays open.
